name: Gryphons

unlocks.name: Bigger and Badder
unlocks.notes: Allows superior Slayer monsters, including Dire gryphons, to spawn while on task.

unlocks.name: Wings Spread
unlocks.notes: Allows Nieve/Steve and Duradel/Kuradal to assign Gryphons.

unlocks.name: Gryphon and on
unlocks.notes: Increases the number of Gryphons assigned by 80.

variantInfo.name: Gryphon
notes: Standard variant.
Requires 51 Slayer to kill and completion of Troubled Tortugans plus 45 Sailing access to the Great Conch.
Attacks with melee crush and has a knockback special if equipped weight is too low.
Normal Gryphons need roughly 30 kg equipped weight to avoid the special damage and instead stun the Gryphon.
Has a 50% elemental weakness to air spells, though melee is typically stronger.

variantInfo.name: Dire gryphon
notes: Superior slayer monster variant that can spawn after purchasing Bigger and Badder.
Has mechanics similar to the boss variant and requires a tortugan shield to nullify guaranteed damage after every hit.
Uses the same 40 kg equipped-weight threshold as the boss for the knockback special.
Cannonable and has a similar drop table to normal Gryphons.

variantInfo.name: Shellbane Gryphon
notes: Boss variant.
Found in the central lair on the Great Conch and only attackable on task.
Solo instanced boss with melee, ranged attacks, and two avoidable special attacks.
For more information on killing the Shellbane Gryphon, see Shellbane Gryphon/Strategies.

locationComparison.name: Western gryphon dungeon
notes: The western cave on the Great Conch.
Contains 18 gryphons and may be fought off task.
Has a southern room that is multicombat and cannonable.
The task page includes a west cave safespot image that avoids all attacks.

locationComparison.name: Eastern gryphon dungeon
notes: Task-only eastern cave on the Great Conch.
Contains 18 gryphons.
Task-only. The south-west part of the dungeon is multicombat and cannonable, while the rest is single-way combat.
Recommended task location with venator bow and dwarf multicannon.

locationComparison.name: Shellbane Gryphon Cave
notes: Task-only boss.
Central Great Conch lair leading to the Shellbane Gryphon.
Solo instanced boss encounter.
Use Shellbane Gryphon/Strategies for boss-specific mechanics.

taskNotes: Gryphons require 51 Slayer and completion of Troubled Tortugans.
The Great Conch access requires 45 Sailing, as described on the Gryphon monster page.
Vannaka and Chaeldar can assign Gryphons after Troubled Tortugans without a points unlock.
Wings Spread costs 80 Slayer points and allows Nieve/Steve and Duradel/Kuradal to assign Gryphons.
For players seeking Gryphon tasks, Vannaka is recommended because Gryphons are Vannaka's highest weighted task even though his amount is lower than Duradel's.
Gryphons are found exclusively on The Great Conch in a western cavern, eastern task-only cavern, and the central Shellbane Gryphon Cave.
Both eastern and western caverns have a southern room that is multicombat and cannonable.
Gryphons attack with melee and have a special attack that causes knockback and moderate damage if equipped weight is too low.
The equipped weight threshold is 30 kg for normal gryphons and 40 kg for the boss.
If the weight threshold is met, the Gryphon stuns itself and the player can click the Gryphon within 2 ticks to knock it back and perform one additional attack without attack delay.
Normal Gryphons do not require a tortugan shield.
A tortugan shield is required for Dire gryphons and Shellbane Gryphon; without it their attacks deal frequent moderate damage even through prayer.
Dire gryphons have mechanics similar to the boss variant.
Gryphons are weakest to melee, ideally stabbing attacks, and have a 50% weakness to air spells.
Players not safespotting are recommended to use melee equipment.
Gryphons are best killed in the south-western multicombat room of the eastern task-only cave using a venator bow and a dwarf multicannon.
A maxed ranged setup can reach 30 kg by using a black mask (i) instead of a Slayer helmet (i), a granite ring, or avernic treads (max) instead of echo boots.
Bring a tortugan shield for the superior, and bring a cannon.
Gryphons have relatively poor drops and players not planning to kill the boss should avoid toggling them on for Nieve or Duradel.
The Shellbane Gryphon has somewhat lackluster drops too, but is slightly better compared to normal Gryphons.
On task, Horn of plenty (empty) improves from 1/2500 to 1/1000 on regular Gryphons.
recommendedMethod: Use the eastern task-only cave's south-west multicombat room with Venator bow and dwarf multicannon. Keep at least 30 kg equipped weight for normal Gryphons and bring a tortugan shield for Dire gryphons or Shellbane Gryphon.
